Approved in the US.
US food use is subject to the listed CFR provisions and their conditions, checked in 2026.
No current country-wide food-use ban was confirmed in the regulatory sources checked in 2026.
The permissions checked in 2026 apply only to the specified preparations, food uses and conditions.
more_info.overview: Oxystearin is a mixture of glycerides containing partially oxidised stearic and other fatty acids. It is produced by controlled heating of hydrogenated cottonseed or soybean oil in air with a suitable catalyst. In the specified food uses it controls crystallisation and helps food release from processing surfaces. The US applications are in vegetable oils and shortenings, with a maximum of 0.125% of the oil or shortening weight.
more_info.origin: Manufactured by heating hydrogenated cottonseed or soybean oil in air under controlled catalytic conditions. The treatment partially oxidises the fatty-acid glycerides. The starting oils in the FDA definition are plant-derived, while the finished additive is chemically processed.
